title: Zscaler's Terraform modules for Cloud Connector on AWS: examples, defaults, FIPS, Transit Gateway

prose.text: The repository is Zscaler's reference IaC for AWS: submodules per resource group and complete examples that call them. It does not configure the Zscaler side; the provider is covered by [[cloud-connector.terraform.provider-behavior]].

prose.label: Scope.
prose.text: {{repo-scope}} {{greenfield}} {{brownfield}} Help and the README disagree on whether Terraform deployments include a bastion {{divergence:bastion-scope}}.

prose.label: The zsec helper.
prose.text: {{zsec-counts}} Autoscaling size limits differ between the module, the examples and zsec: [[cloud-connector.aws.autoscaling]].

checks.do: Which example the deployment came from, since greenfield examples add a bastion and test workloads and the deprecated ones use Lambda route failover instead of GWLB.
For a Transit Gateway hub-and-spoke deployment, whether the hub attachment has appliance mode enabled.
For FIPS, whether the user data carries FIPS_ENABLED=True, since a direct module caller must set it in its own user data.

repo-scope.statement: The AWS Terraform repository creates the resources to deploy and operate Cloud Connector in a new or existing VPC, and its examples directory holds complete automation for greenfield/POV and brownfield/production use.

quotes: Use this repository to create the deployment resources required to deploy and operate Cloud Connector in a new or existing virtual private cloud (VPC).
The [examples](examples/) directory contains complete automation scripts for both greenfield/POV and brownfield/production use.

greenfield.statement: The greenfield templates include a bastion host and test workloads and are designed for greenfield/POV testing.

quotes: These templates include a bastion host and test workloads and are designed for greenfield/POV testing.

brownfield.statement: The brownfield templates are the ones most applicable to production, have more customization options, and deploy no bastion or workload hosts.

quotes: Brownfield deployment templates are most applicable for production deployments and have more customization options than a
They also do not include a bastion or workload hosts deployed.

ex-base.statement: The base example creates the network infrastructure (a VPC, public and workload subnets, an internet gateway and a NAT gateway), one workload server and a bastion host, but no Cloud Connector appliances.

quotes: It does not deploy any Cloud Connector appliances.

Creates 1 new VPC with 1 public subnet and 1 private/workload subnet; 1 IGW; 1 NAT Gateway; 1 Amazon Linux 2023 server workload in the private subnet routing to NAT Gateway; 1 Bastion Host in the public subnet

ex-1cc.statement: base_1cc adds one Cloud Connector private subnet and one Cloud Connector VM routing to the NAT gateway, and repoints the workload subnet route to the Cloud Connector's service ENI.

quotes: Additionally: Creates 1 Cloud Connector private subnet; 1 Cloud Connector VM routing to NAT Gateway; workload private subnet route repointed to service ENI of Cloud Connector.

ex-zpa.statement: The _zpa variants add two Route 53 subnets routing to the Cloud Connector service ENI, a Route 53 outbound resolver endpoint and resolver rules for ZPA DNS redirection.

quotes: Additionally: Creates 2 Route 53 subnets routing to the service ENI of Cloud Connector; Route 53 outbound resolver endpoint; and Route 53 resolver rules for ZPA DNS redirection.

ex-gwlb.statement: base_cc_gwlb creates 4 Cloud Connectors (2 per subnet and AZ), a GWLB that auto-registers their service IPs with health checks, a VPC endpoint service, one GWLB endpoint per Cloud Connector subnet, and workload routes to the GWLB endpoint in the same AZ.

quotes: Additionally: Creates 4 Cloud Connectors (2 per subnet/AZ) routing to NAT Gateway; Gateway Load Balancer auto registers service IPs to target group with health checks; VPC Endpoint Service; 2 GWLB Endpoints (1 in each Cloud Connector subnet); workload private subnet routes pointing to the GWLB Endpoint in their same AZ

ex-gwlb-asg.statement: base_cc_gwlb_asg deploys the Cloud Connectors as an Auto Scaling group with a launch template spanning all Cloud Connector subnets, behind a GWLB with an instance-based target group.

quotes: Cloud Connector Autoscaling Group + Launch Template spanning all CC subnets routing to the NAT Gateway in their same AZ
Gateway Load Balancer with Instance based target group and health checks

ex-brownfield.statement: cc_gwlb (4 Cloud Connector VMs by default, 2 per subnet and AZ) and cc_gwlb_asg (an Auto Scaling group) are the brownfield/production examples, able to reuse an existing VPC, subnets, IGW and NAT gateways and to toggle ZPA/Route 53 resources.

quotes: This deployment type is intended for brownfield/production purposes.
4 Cloud Connector VMs (2 per subnet/AZ) routing to the NAT Gateway in their same AZ
ability to use existing resources (VPC, subnets, IGW, NAT Gateways), toggle ZPA/R53 resources
This deployment type is intended for brownfield/production purposes.
Cloud Connector Autoscaling Group + Launch Template spanning all CC subnets
ability to use existing resources (VPC, subnets, IGW, NAT Gateways), toggle ZPA/R53 resources

ex-deprecated.statement: base_2cc, base_2cc_zpa and cc_ha are marked deprecated; each README says it is only available as reference for legacy users and that Zscaler's recommended deployment method is GWLB. base_2cc and base_2cc_zpa add a second Cloud Connector with a Lambda that fails workload route tables over between the two, and cc_ha can toggle Lambda HA failover.

quotes: (Base_2cc) (deprecated)
This is only available as reference for legacy users. Zscaler's recommended deployment method is Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB)
Creates a second Cloud Connector in a new subnet/Availability Zone wwith Lambda configured for HA failover of workload route tables between the two Cloud Connectors
# Zscaler Starter Deployment Template with HA and ZPA (Base_2cc_zpa) (deprecated)
This is only available as reference for legacy users. Zscaler's recommended deployment method is Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB)
Creates a second Cloud Connector in a new subnet/Availability Zone wwith Lambda configured for HA failover of workload route tables between the two Cloud Connectors
# Zscaler Custom Deployment Template with HA (cc_ha) (deprecated)
This is only available as reference for legacy users. Zscaler's recommended deployment method is Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB)
toggle ZPA/R53 and Lambda HA failover features

network-defaults.statement: The network module defaults `vpc_cidr` to 10.1.0.0/16 and derives all subnets from it, and defaults `az_count` to 2 with validation limiting it to 1 through 3.

quotes: variable "vpc_cidr" { type = string description = "VPC IP CIDR Range.
All subnet resources that might get created (public, workload, cloud connector) are derived from this /16 CIDR.
description = "Default number of subnets to create based on availability zone input" default = 2
Input az_count must be set to a single value between 1 and 3.

tgw-mode.statement: Release 1.5.0 added Transit Gateway hub-and-spoke inspection to base_cc_gwlb and cc_gwlb: `tgw_enabled` (default false) deploys a hub VPC with the Cloud Connectors and GWLB and two spoke VPCs whose traffic the Transit Gateway forwards to the hub.

quotes: feat: add Transit Gateway Hub-and-Spoke inspection support to `base_cc_gwlb` and `cc_gwlb` examples

New variable `tgw_enabled` (default `false`): when set to `true`, deploys a three-VPC TGW hub-and-spoke topology. The hub VPC hosts Cloud Connectors and the GWLB; two spoke VPCs contain workload instances whose traffic is forwarded to the hub for centralized inspection via the Transit Gateway.

tgw-appliance-mode.statement: The Transit Gateway module enables appliance mode on the hub attachment because, per its README, without it TGW may return traffic through a different AZ, breaking GWLB flow stickiness and letting traffic bypass Cloud Connector inspection.

quotes: appliance_mode_support = "enable"

this is required for GWLB-based inspection. Without it, TGW may route return traffic through a different AZ ENI than the original flow, breaking GWLB's 5-tuple flow stickiness and causing traffic to bypass Cloud Connector inspection.

fips-variable.statement: Release 1.5.1 added a `fips_enabled` variable to the Cloud Connector examples that enables FIPS mode through user data; it takes the strings "False" (default) or "True" and is written as FIPS_ENABLED.

quotes: add new `fips_enabled` variable for enabling FIPS mode via userdata in Cloud Connector examples
Enable FIPS mode for Cloud Connector provisioning. Supported values are 'False' or 'True'.
default = "False"
FIPS_ENABLED=${var.fips_enabled}

fips-zsec.statement: The zsec helper asks whether to enable FIPS mode and exports `TF_VAR_fips_enabled` as 'True' or 'False'.

quotes: Enable FIPS mode for this Cloud Connector deployment? (yes/no):
echo "export TF_VAR_fips_enabled='True'" >> .zsecrc
echo "export TF_VAR_fips_enabled='False'" >> .zsecrc

fips-examples-only.statement: FIPS is an example-level input: every Cloud Connector example declares `fips_enabled` while the base example (no Cloud Connector) and the CCVM and ASG modules do not, so a caller of the modules directly must put FIPS_ENABLED in its own user data.
fips-examples-only.conditions: Rests on a search of every examples/*/variables.tf and modules/*/variables.tf at the pin for variable "fips_enabled": present in base_1cc, base_1cc_zpa, base_2cc, base_2cc_zpa, base_cc_gwlb, base_cc_gwlb_asg, base_cc_gwlb_asg_zpa, base_cc_gwlb_zpa, cc_gwlb, cc_gwlb_asg and cc_ha; absent from base and from every module.

zsec-counts.statement: zsec accepts 1 to 20 for the static Cloud Connector count and 1 to 10 for the Auto Scaling group minimum and maximum.

quotes: if ((cc_count >= 1 && cc_count <= 20)); then

bastion-scope.summary: Whether a Terraform deployment of Cloud Connector includes a bastion host.

positions.says: When Terraform configures new appliances, a bastion host is created automatically for management and troubleshooting.

quotes: When using Terraform to configure new appliances, a Bastion host is automatically created for management and troubleshooting purposes.

positions.says: Only the greenfield templates include a bastion; the brownfield templates do not deploy a bastion or workload hosts.

quotes: They also do not include a bastion or workload hosts deployed.

bastion-scope.impact: Troubleshooting guidance that assumes a Terraform bastion for CLI access fails for brownfield deployments; use SSM or a management-interface elastic IP instead.
